title.zh: 卷二百四十六 列傳第五 宗室三
title.raw: 卷二百四十六 列傳第五 宗室三 Volume 246 Biographies 5: Imperial Clan 3

sentences.zh: 英宗四子：長神宗，次吳榮王顥，次潤王顏，次益端獻王頵，皆宣仁聖烈高皇后出也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong had four sons: the eldest was Emperor Shenzong, the second was Prince Wu Rong Wang Hao, the third was Prince Run Wang Yan, the fourth was Prince Yi Duan Xian Wang Yun — all were born of Empress Xuanren the Sagely and Severe Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong had four sons: the eldest became Emperor Shenzong; next came Prince Wu Rong, Hao; then Prince Run, Yan; and lastly Prince Yi, Duan Xian Wang Yun. All were children of Empress Xuanren the Sagely and Severe.

sentences.zh: 顏早亡，徽宗賜名追封。

translations.literal: Yan died early; Emperor Huizong granted a name and conferred posthumous enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan died young; Emperor Huizong bestowed a name and enfeoffed him posthumously.

sentences.zh: 吳榮王顥

translations.literal: Prince Wu Rong, Hao
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Rong, Hao

sentences.zh: 吳榮王顥字仲明，初名仲糺，自右內率府副率為和州防禦使，封安樂郡公，轉明州觀察使，進祁國公。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Rong Wang Hao, courtesy name Zhongming, original name Zhongjiu, from Deputy Director of the Right Inner Rate Office became Defender of He Prefecture, was enfeoffed as Duke of Anle Commandery, transferred to Military Commissioner of Observation for Ming Prefecture, and was promoted to Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Rong, Hao — courtesy name Zhongming, born Zhongjiu — rose from deputy director of the Right Inner Rate Office to defender of He Prefecture, was made Duke of Anle Commandery, then military commissioner of observation for Ming, and was promoted to Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，加檢校太傅、保寧軍節度使、同中書門下平章 事，封東陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, he was added as Grand Tutor with honorary title, Military Commissioner of the Baoning Army, and Co-Governor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping (1064), he received the honorary rank of grand tutor, the post of military commissioner of the Baoning Army, and the title of co-governor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，出閣。

translations.literal: In the third year, he left the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he left the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，進封昌王；

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended, he was advanced to Prince of Chang;
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Hao was promoted to Prince of Chang;

sentences.zh: 官制行，冊拜司空，徙王雍。

translations.literal: When the official system was implemented, he was invested by edict as Minister of Works and transferred to Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After the new official system took effect, he was formally invested as Minister of Works and made Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嗣位，加太保，換成德、橫海二鎮，徙封揚王，賜讚拜不名，五日一謁禁中。

translations.literal: When Zhezong succeeded, he was added as Grand Guardian, exchanged to the two circuits of Chengde and Henghai, transferred to Prince of Yang, granted the privilege of bowing without having his name called, and visited the Forbidden City once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong succeeded, Hao was made grand guardian, given the Chengde and Henghai circuits, and raised to Prince of Yang. He was granted the privilege of being addressed without naming him and was to enter the Forbidden City every five days.

sentences.zh: 帝致恭如家人禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed him respect as in family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with the deference due within a family.

sentences.zh: 神宗祔廟，拜太傅，移鎮京兆、鳳翔。

translations.literal: When Shenzong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, Hao was appointed Grand Tutor and transferred to the Jingzhao and Fengxiang circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong was installed in the ancestral temple, Hao was made grand tutor and given the Jingzhao and Fengxiang circuits.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來，顥屢請居外，章上輒卻。

translations.literal: From the Xining era onward, Hao repeatedly requested to reside outside the palace; each memorial submitted was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining era on, Hao repeatedly asked to live outside the palace, but every petition was turned down.

sentences.zh: 至元祐初，乃賜咸宜坊第一區，榜曰「親賢」與弟頵對 邸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, he was granted the foremost residence in Xianyi Ward, with a plaque reading "Intimate Worthies," facing his younger brother Yun's mansion across the lane.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, he was given the finest house in Xianyi Ward, labeled "Intimate Worthies," directly opposite his younger brother Yun's residence.

sentences.zh: 車駕偕三宮臨幸，留宴終日。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage, together with the three palaces, visited in person and remained feasting the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came with the three palaces to visit in person and stayed for a feast that lasted the entire day.

sentences.zh: 拜太尉，諸子皆命賜官，制曰：「先皇帝篤兄弟之好，以恩勝義，不許二叔出居於外，蓋武王待周公之意。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Commandant, and all his sons were ordered to receive granted offices. The edict said: "The late emperor was devoted to brotherly affection, letting favor prevail over propriety and not permitting his two uncles to live outside — this was the meaning of King Wu's treatment of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was appointed grand commandant, and all his sons were granted offices. The edict read: "The late emperor cherished brotherly affection, letting kindness outweigh ritual propriety by not allowing his two uncles to live outside the palace — in the spirit of how King Wu treated the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后嚴朝廷之禮， 以義制恩，始從其請，出就外宅，得孔子遠其子之意。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was strict about court ritual, using propriety to restrain favor, and only then acceded to his request to leave and take up an outer residence — attaining Confucius's meaning in keeping one's son at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager upheld court ritual, using propriety to curb excessive favor, and only then granted his request to move to an outer residence — in the spirit of Confucius keeping his son at a distance.

sentences.zh: 二聖不同，同歸於道，皆可以為萬世法。

translations.literal: The two sages differed, yet both returned to the Way; each may serve as a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The two sovereigns acted differently, yet both embodied the Way; either course may stand as a model for all time.

sentences.zh: 朕承侍兩宮，按行新第，顧瞻懷思，潸然出涕。

translations.literal: We have attended upon the two palaces, inspected the new residence, looked back in remembrance, and shed tears in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: As I have served the two palaces and walked through this new residence, looking back stirs deep feeling, and tears flow unbidden.

sentences.zh: 昔漢明帝問東平王：『在家何以為樂？

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Ming of Han asked the Prince of Dongping: "At home, what brings the greatest joy?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Ming of Han asked the Prince of Dongping, "What is the greatest joy at home?

sentences.zh: 』王言：『為善最樂。

translations.literal: " The prince replied: "Doing good is the greatest joy.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince answered, "Doing good is the greatest joy.

sentences.zh: 』帝大其言，因送列侯印十九枚，諸子五歲以上悉佩之，著之簡策，天下不以為私。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly approved his words and therefore sent nineteen marquis seals; all sons five years of age and above wore them alike, recorded in the bamboo annals, and the realm did not regard it as favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply impressed and sent nineteen marquis seals; every son five or older was to wear one. The act was recorded for posterity, and the realm did not see it as private favor.

sentences.zh: 今王諸子性於忠孝，漸於禮義，自勝衣以上，頎然皆有成人之風，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Now the prince's sons are by nature devoted to loyalty and filial piety, steeped in ritual and righteousness; from those who have reached the age to wear full garments upward, each tall and stately bears the bearing of a grown man — We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Your sons are naturally loyal and filial and are growing steeped in ritual and righteousness. From those old enough to wear full garments, each already carries himself like a grown man — a quality I greatly admire.

sentences.zh: 其各進一官，以助其為善之樂，尚勉之哉！

translations.literal: Let each advance one rank, to assist their joy in doing good — strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Let each of them advance one rank, to support their joy in doing good. Press on!

sentences.zh: 毋忝父祖，以為邦家光。

translations.literal: Do not disgrace father and forebears, and be a glory to the state and house.
translations.idiomatic: Do not dishonor your father and forebears; bring honor to the realm and the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 」徙封徐王，詔書不名。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Prince of Xu; edicts did not call his name.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Prince of Xu, and edicts no longer named him when addressing him.

sentences.zh: 顥天資穎異，尤嗜學，始就外傅，每一經終，即遺講讀官以器幣服馬。

translations.literal: Hao was by nature exceptionally keen and especially fond of learning. When he first took an outer tutor, at the completion of each classic he would send the lecturing reader vessels, silks, robes, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was exceptionally gifted and devoted to study. Once he took an outside tutor, he rewarded the lecturing reader with vessels, silks, robes, and horses whenever he finished a classic.

sentences.zh: 工飛白，善射，好圖書，博求善本。

translations.literal: He was skilled in feibai script, adept at archery, loved books, and widely sought fine editions.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at feibai calligraphy and archery, loved books, and searched widely for fine editions.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘉其志尚，每得異書，亟馳使以示。

translations.literal: Shenzong commended his aspirations; whenever he obtained a rare book, he would quickly dispatch a messenger to show it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong admired his scholarly bent and, whenever he came upon a rare book, would quickly send a courier to show it to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜方團玉帶，俾服而朝，顥辭，乃為製玉魚以別之。

translations.literal: He was once granted a square round jade belt and ordered to wear it at court; Hao declined, so a jade fish ornament was made instead to distinguish him.
translations.idiomatic: He was once given a square round jade belt and told to wear it at court, but Hao declined; the emperor then had a jade fish made to distinguish him instead.

sentences.zh: 是後親王遂踵為故實。

translations.literal: Thereafter imperial princes followed this as established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After that, imperial princes followed this as established custom.

sentences.zh: 初，居英宗喪，丐解官終制，以厭於至尊，不克遂。

translations.literal: At first, during mourning for Yingzong, he begged to resign office and observe the full mourning term, but because this displeased the supreme sovereign, he could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while mourning Yingzong, he asked to resign and observe the full mourning period, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 服慈聖光獻太后之服，易月當除，顥曰：「身為孫而情文缺然，若是可乎？

translations.literal: When wearing mourning for Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng the Luminous and Offering, the month for changing garments arrived and mourning should have ended. Hao said: "As a grandson, yet with feeling and form lacking — can this be right?
translations.idiomatic: When mourning Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng the Luminous and Offering, the month came to change garments and end mourning. Hao said, "I am her grandson, yet the proper feeling and form are incomplete — can this be acceptable?

sentences.zh: 請如心喪禮，須上禫除，即吉。

translations.literal: I request to follow the heart-mourning rites and not return to normal dress until the upper end-of-mourning removal.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to follow heart-mourning rites and not return to normal dress until the upper end-of-mourning ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 子孝騫嗣，終寧國軍節度使、晉康郡王；

translations.literal: His son Xiaojian succeeded, ending as Military Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and Prince of Jinkang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaojian succeeded him, ending as military commissioner of the Ningguo Army and Prince of Jinkang Commandery;

sentences.zh: 孝錫終嘉州團練使，贈永國公。

translations.literal: Xiaoxi ended as Regimentation Commissioner of Jia Prefecture and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxi ended as regimentation commissioner of Jia Prefecture and was posthumously made Duke of Yong.

sentences.zh: 益端獻王頵

translations.literal: Prince Yi Duan Xian, Yun
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi, Duan Xian Wang Yun

sentences.zh: 頵端重明粹，少好學，長博通群書，工飛白、篆籀。

translations.literal: Yun was dignified, weighty, bright, and pure; in youth he loved learning, and in maturity he mastered many books, skilled in feibai and seal scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was grave, bright, and refined. He loved learning as a youth and in maturity mastered many books, excelling at feibai and seal scripts.

sentences.zh: 賓接宮僚，歲滿當去，輒奏留，久者至十餘年。

translations.literal: He received palace staff as guests; when their term was complete and they should depart, he would memorialize to retain them — some for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained palace staff as guests; when their terms ended, he would petition to keep them — some for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 頗好醫書，手著《普惠集效方》，且儲藥以救病者。

translations.literal: He was quite fond of medical books, personally composed the Collected Effective Prescriptions of Universal Benefit, and also stored medicines to treat the sick.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of medical books, personally wrote Collected Effective Prescriptions of Universal Benefit, and kept medicines on hand to treat the sick.

sentences.zh: 子九人：孝哲，右驍衛將軍，早亡；

translations.literal: He had nine sons: Xiaozhe, General of the Right Valiant Cavalry, died early;
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons: Xiaozhe, general of the Right Valiant Cavalry, who died young;

sentences.zh: 孝奕，彰化軍節度觀察留後，贈司空、平原郡王；

translations.literal: Xiaoyi, Acting Military Commissioner of Observation for the Zhanghua Army, posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Prince of Pingyuan Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi, acting military commissioner of observation for the Zhanghua Army, posthumously made Minister of Works and Prince of Pingyuan Commandery;

sentences.zh: 孝參，奉國軍節度使，改寧武、武勝，封豫章郡王；

translations.literal: Xiaocan, Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army, transferred to Ningwu and Wusheng, enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaocan, military commissioner of the Fengguo Army, later given Ningwu and Wusheng, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang Commandery;

sentences.zh: 孝永，邢州觀察使，贈司空、廣陵郡王；

translations.literal: Xiaoyong, Military Commissioner of Observation for Xing Prefecture, posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Prince of Guangling Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyong, military commissioner of observation for Xing Prefecture, posthumously made Minister of Works and Prince of Guangling Commandery;

sentences.zh: 孝詒、孝騭、孝悅、孝穎、孝願，皆至節度使。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi, Xiaoji, Xiaoyue, Xiaoying, and Xiaoyuan all reached the rank of military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi, Xiaoji, Xiaoyue, Xiaoying, and Xiaoyuan all rose to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳榮穆王佖

translations.literal: Prince Wu Rong the Solemn, Bian
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Rong the Solemn, Bian

sentences.zh: 燕王俁

translations.literal: Prince of Yan, You
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan, You

sentences.zh: 紹興初，有崔紹祖者至壽春府，稱越王次子，受上皇蠟詔為天下兵馬大元帥，興師恢復。

translations.literal: Early in Shaoxing, one Cui Shaozu came to Shouchun Prefecture, claiming to be the second son of the Prince of Yue, having received a wax-sealed edict from the Retired Emperor appointing him Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven to raise troops and recover the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing, a man named Cui Shaozu arrived at Shouchun Prefecture, claiming to be the Prince of Yue's second son. He said he held a wax-sealed edict from the retired emperor making him grand marshal of all armies under heaven to raise troops and restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫使趙霖以聞。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhao Lin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Zhao Lin reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，事敗，送臺獄伏罪，斬於越州市。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the mobile court; the affair failed, he was sent to the censorial prison to confess guilt, and was beheaded in Yuezhou City.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the mobile court, but the plot failed. He was sent to the censorial prison, confessed, and was beheaded in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 楚榮憲王似

translations.literal: Prince Chu Rong the Worthy, Si
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chu Rong the Worthy, Si

sentences.zh: 左司諫江公望上疏，以為：「親隙不可開，開則言可離貳；

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Bureau Adviser Jiang Gongwang submitted a memorial, stating: "Rifts among kin must not be opened; once opened, words may lead to divided loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Left remonstrance bureau adviser Jiang Gongwang submitted a memorial arguing that "rifts among kin must not be opened, for once opened, words can breed divided loyalty;

sentences.zh: 疑跡不可顯，顯則事難磨滅。

translations.literal: suspicious traces must not be displayed; once displayed, affairs are hard to erase.
translations.idiomatic: and suspicious traces must not be displayed, for once displayed, affairs are hard to erase.

sentences.zh: 陛下之得天下也，章惇嘗持異議，已有隙跡矣。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty gained the realm, Zhang Dun once held a dissenting view — a rift and trace already existed.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty gained the throne, Zhang Dun had once held a dissenting view — a rift and trace already existed.

sentences.zh: 蔡王出於無心，年尚幼小，未達禍亂之萌，恬不以為恤。

translations.literal: Prince Cai acted without ulterior motive; he was still young and had not grasped the sprouting of calamity and disorder, calmly taking no concern.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cai acted without ulterior motive. He was still young and did not grasp how calamity begins, and took no alarm.

sentences.zh: 陛下一切包容，已開之隙復塗，已顯之跡復泯矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fully embraced all, resealing rifts already opened and effacing traces already displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty fully embraced him, resealing rifts already opened and effacing traces already shown.

sentences.zh: 恩意渥縟，歡然不失兄弟之情。

translations.literal: Favor and affection were thick and abundant; joyfully brotherly feeling was not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Favor ran deep, and brotherly feeling remained intact.

sentences.zh: 若以曖昧無根之語，加諸至親骨肉之間，則有魏文『相煎太急』之譏，而忘大舜親愛之道，豈治世之美事邪。

translations.literal: If vague words without foundation are applied between the closest flesh and blood, there will be the reproach of Wei Wen's "boiling each other too urgently," forgetting Great Shun's way of affection among kin — how can this be a fine affair of a well-governed age?
translations.idiomatic: If vague, groundless words are applied between the closest kin, you invite the reproach of Wei Wen's "boiling each other too urgently" and forget Great Shun's way of affection — how can that be fitting in a well-governed age?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下密詔有司，凡無根之言勿形案牘，倘有瑕可指，一人胸次，則終身不忘，跡不可泯，隙不可塗，則骨肉離矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty secretly to instruct the offices: all words without foundation must not appear in case documents. If there is a flaw that can be pointed to, once it enters one person's breast, it is never forgotten for life — traces cannot be effaced, rifts cannot be resealed, and flesh and blood are parted.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty secretly to instruct the offices that groundless words must never appear in official documents. Once a flaw is noted, it lodges in a man's heart forever — traces cannot be erased, rifts cannot be resealed, and kin are parted.

sentences.zh: 一有浸淫旁及蔡王之語，不識陛下將何以處之，陛下何顏見神考於太廟乎？

translations.literal: Once words seeping by degrees reach Prince Cai, I do not know how Your Majesty will deal with it — with what face will Your Majesty meet Emperor Shenzong in the ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: Once rumors seep outward and touch Prince Cai, how will Your Majesty handle it? With what face will you meet Emperor Shenzong in the ancestral temple?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，公望罷知淮陽軍。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Gongwang was dismissed to know the Huaiyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Gongwang was dismissed to military commissioner of the Huaiyang Army.

sentences.zh: 徽宗雖出公望，然頗思其言，止治其左右。

translations.literal: Although Huizong removed Gongwang, he quite reflected on his words and only punished those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Huizong removed Gongwang, he took his words to heart and punished only those around the prince.

sentences.zh: 獻湣太子茂

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xian the Lamented, Mao
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xian the Lamented, Mao

sentences.zh: 哲宗一子：獻湣太子茂，昭懷劉皇后為賢妃時所生。

translations.literal: Zhezong had one son: Crown Prince Xian the Lamented Mao, born when Empress Zhaohuai Liu was still Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong had one son: Crown Prince Xian the Lamented, Mao, born when Empress Zhaohuai Liu was still a worthy consort.

sentences.zh: 帝未有子，而中宮虛位，后因是得立。

translations.literal: The emperor had no son, and the central palace seat was vacant; the empress therefore was able to be established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no son and the empress's seat was vacant, so the consort was elevated on that basis.

sentences.zh: 然才三月而夭，追封越王，諡衝獻。

translations.literal: Yet after only three months he died young; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yue, posthumous title Chongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he died after only three months. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yue with the posthumous title Chongxian.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，改諡獻湣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, the posthumous title was changed to Xianmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning (1102), his posthumous title was changed to Xian the Lamented.

sentences.zh: 后之立也， 鄒浩凡三上疏諫，隨削其稿。

translations.literal: When the empress was established, Zou Hao thrice submitted memorials remonstrating; each draft was struck down as it came.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was installed, Zou Hao submitted three memorials in protest, and each draft was suppressed as it arrived.

sentences.zh: 至是，或謂浩有「殺卓氏而奪其子，欺人可也，詎可以欺天乎」之語，徽宗昭暴其事，復竄浩昭州，而峻茂典冊。

translations.literal: At this time, some said Hao had the words "Kill the Zhuo clan and seize her son — one may deceive men, but how can one deceive Heaven?" Huizong publicly exposed the affair, again banished Hao to Zhaozhou, and made Mao's canonical rites severe and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Now some claimed Hao had said, "Kill the Zhuo clan and seize her son — you may deceive men, but how can you deceive Heaven?" Huizong publicly exposed the affair, banished Hao again to Zhaozhou, and made Mao's canonical rites especially grand.

sentences.zh: 後上表謝，然浩蓋無是言也。

translations.literal: The empress submitted a memorial of thanks, yet Hao in fact had no such words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress submitted a memorial of thanks, but Hao had never spoken those words.

sentences.zh: 鄆王楷

translations.literal: Prince of Yun, Kai
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yun, Kai

sentences.zh: 鄆王楷，帝第三子。

translations.literal: Prince of Yun Kai was the emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yun, Kai, was the emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 初名煥。

translations.literal: His original name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Huan.

sentences.zh: 始封魏國公，進高密郡王、嘉王，歷奉寧、鎮安、鎮東、武寧、保平、荊南、寧江、劍南西川、鎮南、河東、寧海十一節度使。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, advanced to Prince of Gaomi Commandery and Prince of Jia, and successively held the eleven military commissioner posts of Fengning, Zhen'an, Zhendong, Wuning, Baoping, Jingnan, Ningjiang, Jiannan Xichuan, Zhennan, Hedong, and Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made Duke of Wei, then Prince of Gaomi Commandery and Prince of Jia, and in turn held eleven military commissioner posts: Fengning, Zhen'an, Zhendong, Wuning, Baoping, Jingnan, Ningjiang, Jiannan Xichuan, Zhennan, Hedong, and Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 政和八年，廷策進士，唱名第一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenghe, in the palace examination for presented scholars, he was called first in the roll.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenghe (1118), he took the palace examination for presented scholars and was called first on the roll.

sentences.zh: 母王妃方有寵，遂超拜太傅，改王鄆，仍提舉皇城司。

translations.literal: His mother the princess consort had just gained favor, so he was promoted beyond precedent to Grand Tutor, transferred to Prince of Yun, and still supervised the Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His mother the princess consort had just won favor, so he was promoted beyond precedent to grand tutor, made Prince of Yun, and continued to supervise the Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出入禁省，不復限朝暮，於外第作飛橋復道以通往來。

translations.literal: He entered and left the Forbidden Offices without limit of morning or evening; at his outer residence he built flying bridges and elevated passages for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: He came and went from the Forbidden Offices without regard to time of day and built flying bridges and elevated walkways at his outer residence for constant access.

sentences.zh: 北伐之役，且將以為元帥，會白溝失利而止。

translations.literal: In the northern campaign, he was about to be made commander-in-chief, but when defeat came at Baigou it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign he was about to be made commander-in-chief, but the plan was dropped after defeat at Baigou.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，改鎮鳳翔、彰德軍。

translations.literal: When Qinzong ascended, he was transferred to the Fengxiang and Zhangde armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong ascended, Kai was given the Fengxiang and Zhangde armies.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，與諸王皆北遷。

translations.literal: Early in Jingkang, together with all the princes he was moved north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingkang (1126), he was moved north with the other princes.

sentences.zh: 肅王樞

translations.literal: Prince Su, Shu
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su, Shu

sentences.zh: 肅王樞，帝第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Su Shu was the emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su, Shu, was the emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初封吳國公，進建安郡王、肅王，歷節度六鎮。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, advanced to Prince of Jian'an Commandery and Prince Su, and successively held six military commissioner posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made Duke of Wu, then Prince of Jian'an Commandery and Prince Su, and held six military commissioner posts in turn.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金人圍京城，要帝子弟為質，且求輸兩河。

translations.literal: Early in Jingkang, the Jurchens besieged the capital, demanding the emperor's sons and younger brothers as hostages and also demanding the surrender of the Two He regions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingkang, the Jurchens besieged the capital, demanding imperial sons and brothers as hostages and tribute from the Two He regions.

sentences.zh: 於是遣宰臣張邦昌從樞使斡離不軍，為金人所留，約俟割地畢遣還，而挾以北去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chancellor Zhang Bangchang was sent to follow Prince Su to the army of the Jin commander Wanyan Zonghan; he was detained by the Jin, with the agreement that after the land cession was complete he would be sent back — yet they were taken north.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent chancellor Zhang Bangchang with Prince Shu to the army of the Jin commander Wanyan Zonghan. Both were detained by the Jin on the promise they would return once the land cession was complete, but were taken north instead.

sentences.zh: 景王杞

translations.literal: Prince Jing, Qi
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing, Qi

sentences.zh: 景王杞，初授武安軍節度使、檢校太尉，封冀國公。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Qi was first appointed Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and Grand Commandant with honorary title, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing, Qi, was first appointed military commissioner of the Wu'an Army and honorary grand commandant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，改授山南東道節度使，加開府儀同三司，封文安郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, added as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wen'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daguan (1108), he was made military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wen'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 政和中，授檢校太保，尋遷太保，改授護國、武昌軍節度使，追封景王。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era, he was appointed Grand Guardian with honorary title, soon transferred to Grand Guardian, transferred to Military Commissioner of the Huguo and Wuchang armies, and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he was made honorary grand guardian, then grand guardian, then military commissioner of the Huguo and Wuchang armies, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，授荊南、鎮東軍節度使，遷太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Jingnan and Zhendong armies and transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang (1126), he was given the Jingnan and Zhendong armies and promoted to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣詣金營充賀正旦使。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was sent to the Jin camp as envoy to congratulate the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was sent to the Jin camp as envoy for the New Year congratulations.

sentences.zh: 既歸，又從上幸青城。

translations.literal: After returning, he again followed the emperor in visiting Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, he again accompanied the emperor to Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 及上皇出郊，杞日侍左右，衣不解帶，食不食肉，上皇製發願文，述祈天請命之意，以授杞。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor went out to the suburbs, Qi attended him day by day at his side, not loosening his belt, not eating meat. The Retired Emperor composed a vow text setting forth the meaning of praying Heaven and begging for fate, and gave it to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor went out to the suburbs, Qi attended him daily, never loosening his belt and eating no meat. The retired emperor wrote a vow text expressing his plea to Heaven for deliverance and gave it to Qi.

sentences.zh: 杞頓首泣。

translations.literal: Qi bowed his head to the ground and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Qi prostrated himself and wept.

sentences.zh: 及北行，鬚髮盡白。

translations.literal: When they went north, his beard and hair turned entirely white.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they went north, his hair and beard had turned completely white.

sentences.zh: 濟王栩

translations.literal: Prince of Ji, Xu
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ji, Xu

sentences.zh: 同景王杞為賀金人正旦使。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Jing Qi he served as envoy to congratulate the Jurchen New Year.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Prince Jing, Qi, as envoy to congratulate the Jurchen New Year.

sentences.zh: 既還，又與何㮚為請命使，金帥紿栩曰：「自古有南即有北，不可相無，今所欲割地而已。

translations.literal: After returning, he again with He Li served as envoy to beg for mercy. The Jin commander deceived Xu, saying: "From antiquity, where there is south there is north — they cannot exist without each other; what is sought now is only the cession of territory.
translations.idiomatic: After returning, he went again with He Li as envoy to plead for mercy. The Jin commander deceived Xu, saying, "From antiquity, where there is a south there is a north — neither can exist without the other. All we seek now is the cession of territory.

sentences.zh: 」栩回以白上，且言金帥請與上皇相見，上曰：「豈可使上皇蒙塵。

translations.literal: " Xu returned and reported to the emperor, also saying the Jin commander requested to meet the Retired Emperor. The emperor said: "How can we let the Retired Emperor suffer dust and disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: " Xu reported this to the emperor and said the Jin commander wished to meet the retired emperor. The emperor replied, "How can I let the retired emperor suffer such disgrace?

sentences.zh: 」遂自出，以栩從行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went out himself, taking Xu to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went out himself, taking Xu with him.

sentences.zh: 及索諸王家屬，栩夫人曹氏避難他出，徐秉哲捕而拘之，遂同北去。

translations.literal: When the Jin demanded the families of all the princes, Xu's wife Lady Cao had fled elsewhere to escape danger; Xu Bingzhe captured and detained her, and she was taken north together with them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin demanded the families of all the princes, Xu's wife Lady Cao had fled to escape the turmoil. Xu Bingzhe captured and detained her, and she was taken north with them.

sentences.zh: 徐王棣

translations.literal: Prince of Xu, Di
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu, Di

sentences.zh: 徐王棣，初授鎮江軍節度使、檢校太尉，封徐國公。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Di was first appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army and Grand Commandant with honorary title, enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu, Di, was first appointed military commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army and honorary grand commandant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 政和中，授檢校太保。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era, he was appointed Grand Guardian with honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he was made honorary grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，改鎮南軍節度使，加開府儀同三司，封高平郡王。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe era, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, added as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuanhe he was made military commissioner of the Zhennan Army, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋改山南東道、河陽三城節度使，進封徐王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit and the Three Cities of Heyang, and advanced to Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the Shannan East Circuit and the Three Cities of Heyang and promoted to Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 後從淵聖北去。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Captive Sage north.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the captive emperor north.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，有萬州李勃者，偽稱祁王，內侍楊公謹與言徐王起居狀，勃遂改稱徐王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, one Li Bo of Wan Prefecture falsely claimed to be Prince of Qi; the inner attendant Yang Gongjin spoke with him of Prince Xu's daily circumstances, and Bo then changed his claim to Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing (1132), a man named Li Bo of Wan Prefecture falsely claimed to be Prince of Qi. The inner attendant Yang Gongjin discussed Prince Xu's daily circumstances with him, and Bo then claimed to be Prince of Xu instead.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使張浚遣赴行在，上命王府故吏驗視，言非真，詔送大理，情得，棄市。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun sent him to the mobile court; the emperor ordered former officials of the princely household to examine him — they said he was not genuine. An edict sent him to the Court of Judicial Review; the facts were established, and he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Zhang Jun sent him to the mobile court. The emperor ordered former officials of the princely household to examine him; they declared him an impostor. He was sent to the Court of Judicial Review, the case was proved, and he was executed in public.

sentences.zh: 沂王㮙

translations.literal: Prince of Yi, Kai
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi, Kai

sentences.zh: 沂王㮙，初授橫海軍節度使、檢校太尉、冀國公。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Kai was first appointed Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army, Grand Commandant with honorary title, and Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi, Kai, was first appointed military commissioner of the Henghai Army, honorary grand commandant, and Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 政和中，授檢校太保。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era, he was appointed Grand Guardian with honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he was made honorary grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，改劍南西川節度使，加開府儀同三司，封河間郡王。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe era, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jiannan Xichuan, added as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuanhe he was made military commissioner of Jiannan Xichuan, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋改劍南東川、威武軍節度使，遷太保，進封沂王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jiannan Dongchuan and the Weiwu Army, moved to Grand Guardian, and advanced to Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given Jiannan Dongchuan and the Weiwu Army, promoted to grand guardian, and made Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 後從淵聖出郊，至北方，與駙馬劉彥文告上皇左右謀變，金遣人按問，上皇遣莘王植、駙馬蔡鞗等對辨，凡三日，㮙、彥文氣折，金人誅之。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Captive Sage out to the suburbs; reaching the north, together with Imperial Son-in-law Liu Yanwen he reported that those around the Retired Emperor were plotting rebellion. The Jin sent men to investigate; the Retired Emperor sent Prince Xin Zhi, Imperial Son-in-law Cai Bian, and others to argue in rebuttal. After three days Kai and Yanwen were broken in spirit, and the Jurchens executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the captive emperor out to the suburbs. In the north, he and imperial son-in-law Liu Yanwen accused the retired emperor's attendants of plotting rebellion. The Jin investigated; the retired emperor sent Prince Xin, Zhi, imperial son-in-law Cai Bian, and others to rebut the charge. After three days Kai and Yanwen were broken, and the Jurchens executed them.

sentences.zh: 和王栻

translations.literal: Prince He, Shi
translations.idiomatic: Prince He, Shi

sentences.zh: 和王栻，初授靜江軍節度使、檢校太尉、廣國公。

translations.literal: Prince He Shi was first appointed Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, Grand Commandant with honorary title, and Duke of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince He, Shi, was first appointed military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, honorary grand commandant, and Duke of Guang.

sentences.zh: 三年，授檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Grand Guardian with honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made honorary grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 尋改定武軍節度使，加開府儀同三司，封南康郡王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Dingwu Army, added as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made military commissioner of the Dingwu Army, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，授瀛海、安化軍節度使、檢校太傅，追封和王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yinghai and Anhua armies and Grand Tutor with honorary title, and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince He.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was given the Yinghai and Anhua armies and honorary grand tutor, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince He.

sentences.zh: 後從淵聖出郊。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Captive Sage out to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the captive emperor out to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 有遺女一人，高宗朝封樂平縣主，出適杜安石，命大宗正司主婚。

translations.literal: He left behind one daughter; in the Gaozong reign she was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping County, married to Du Anshi, and the Directorate of the Imperial Clan was ordered to preside over the wedding.
translations.idiomatic: He left a daughter who, under Gaozong, was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping County, married Du Anshi, and had the Directorate of the Imperial Clan arrange the wedding.

sentences.zh: 信王榛

translations.literal: Prince Xin, Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin, Zhen

sentences.zh: 信王榛，初授建雄軍節度使、檢校太尉，封福國公。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Zhen was first appointed Military Commissioner of the Jianxiong Army and Grand Commandant with honorary title, enfeoffed as Duke of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin, Zhen, was first appointed military commissioner of the Jianxiong Army and honorary grand commandant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fu.

sentences.zh: 三年，授檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Grand Guardian with honorary title.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made honorary grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，改安遠軍節度使，加開府儀同三司，封平陽郡王。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Anyuan Army, added as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanhe he was made military commissioner of the Anyuan Army, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，授慶陽、昭化軍節度使，遷檢校太傅，進封信王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qingyang and Zhaohua armies, transferred to Grand Tutor with honorary title, and advanced to Prince Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was given the Qingyang and Zhaohua armies, promoted to honorary grand tutor, and made Prince Xin.

sentences.zh: 後從淵聖出郊，北行至慶源，亡匿真定境中。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Captive Sage out to the suburbs; going north as far as Qingyuan, he fled and hid within the borders of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the captive emperor out to the suburbs, but going north as far as Qingyuan he fled and hid in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 時馬廣與趙邦傑聚兵保五馬山砦，陰迎榛歸，奉以為主，兩河遺民聞風響應。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Guang and Zhao Bangjie gathered troops to hold the fortress at Wuma Mountain, secretly welcoming Zhen back and making him their leader; remnant people of the Two He regions responded at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guang and Zhao Bangjie were then holding the fortress at Wuma Mountain with gathered troops, secretly welcoming Zhen back and making him their leader. Remnant populations of the Two He regions rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 榛遣廣詣行在奏之，其略曰：「邦傑與廣，忠義之心，堅若金石，臣自陷賊中，頗知其虛實。

translations.literal: Zhen sent Guang to the mobile court to memorialize, in summary: "Bangjie and Guang have hearts of loyalty and righteousness firm as metal and stone. Since I fell among the bandits, I have come to know their strengths and weaknesses quite well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent Guang to the mobile court with a memorial that read in part: "Bangjie and Guang are loyal and steadfast as metal and stone. Having fallen among the enemy, I know their situation well.

sentences.zh: 賊今稍墮，皆懷歸心，且累敗於西夏，而契丹亦出攻之。

translations.literal: The bandits are now somewhat in decline; all harbor thoughts of returning, and they have suffered repeated defeats by Western Xia, while the Khitans have also come out to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is weakening; many wish to return, they have suffered repeated defeats by Western Xia, and the Khitans are also attacking them.

sentences.zh: 今山西諸砦鄉兵約十餘萬，力與賊抗，但皆苦窘，兼闕戎器。

translations.literal: Now the local militia of the various fortresses in Shanxi number about a hundred thousand or more, striving against the bandits with force, but all suffer hardship and lack, and moreover are short of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The militia of the Shanxi fortresses now number more than a hundred thousand and are fighting the enemy, but they are destitute and lack arms.

sentences.zh: 臣多方存恤，惟望朝廷遣兵來援，不然，久之恐反為賊用。

translations.literal: Your servant has in many ways preserved and comforted them, only hoping the court will send troops to aid — otherwise, in time they may fear turning instead to serve the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: I have done what I can to support them and beg the court to send troops. Otherwise, in time they may be forced to serve the enemy instead.

sentences.zh: 臣於陛下，以禮言則君臣，以義言則兄弟，其憂國念親之心無異。

translations.literal: Between your servant and Your Majesty, by ritual propriety we are ruler and minister, by righteousness we are brothers — the heart that grieves for the state and remembers kin is no different.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual I am your subject; by righteousness I am your brother. My concern for the realm and for our kin is the same as yours.

sentences.zh: 願委臣總大軍，與諸砦鄉兵，約日大舉，決見成功。

translations.literal: I wish to be entrusted with overall command of the great army, together with the local militia of the various fortresses, to launch a major campaign on a set day and assuredly achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be entrusted with overall command of the army and the fortress militias, to strike on a set day and achieve a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 」廣既至，黃潛善、汪伯彥疑其非真，上識榛手書，遂除河外兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: " When Guang arrived, Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan doubted he was genuine, but the emperor recognized Zhen's handwriting and thereupon appointed him Grand Marshal of Armies and Horses Beyond the River.
translations.idiomatic: " When Guang arrived, Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan doubted the message, but the emperor recognized Zhen's handwriting and appointed him grand marshal of armies beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 潛善、伯彥終疑之，廣將行，密授朝旨，使幾察榛，復令廣聽諸路節制。

translations.literal: Qianshan and Boyan remained doubtful to the end. As Guang was about to depart, they secretly conveyed court instructions to watch and investigate Zhen, and again ordered Guang to obey the control of the various circuit commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan and Boyan remained skeptical. As Guang was about to leave, they secretly instructed him to investigate Zhen and ordered him to obey the various circuit commanders.

sentences.zh: 廣知事不成，遂留於大名府不進。

translations.literal: Guang knew the affair could not succeed and therefore remained at Daming Prefecture without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Guang saw the plan could not succeed and stayed at Daming Prefecture without advancing.

sentences.zh: 會有言榛將渡河入京，朝廷因詔擇日還京，以伐其謀。

translations.literal: Just then there were reports that Zhen would cross the river and enter the capital; the court therefore issued an edict fixing a day for his return to the capital, to thwart his design.
translations.idiomatic: Reports then spread that Zhen would cross the river and enter the capital. The court issued an edict fixing a day for his return, to thwart his plans.

sentences.zh: 金人恐廣以援兵至，急發兵攻諸砦，斷其汲道，諸砦遂陷。

translations.literal: The Jurchens feared Guang would bring relief troops and urgently sent troops to attack the various fortresses, cutting off their water routes; the fortresses thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Guang would bring relief troops, the Jurchens attacked the fortresses at once, cut off their water supply, and overran them.

sentences.zh: 榛亡，不知所在，或曰後與上皇同居五國城。

translations.literal: Zhen perished; his whereabouts were unknown. Some say he later dwelt together with the Retired Emperor in the Five States Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen disappeared; his fate was unknown. Some said he later lived with the retired emperor in the Five States Fortress.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，鄧州有楊其姓者，聚千餘人，自稱信王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, in Deng Prefecture one surnamed Yang gathered more than a thousand men and called himself Prince Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing, a man surnamed Yang in Deng Prefecture gathered more than a thousand followers and claimed to be Prince Xin.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫使翟興覺詐，遣將斬之以聞。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhai Xing detected the fraud and sent a general to behead him and report.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Zhai Xing detected the fraud, sent a general to behead him, and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 皇太子諶

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chen
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chen

sentences.zh: 二年，上幸青城，命密院同知孫傅兼太子少傅，吏部侍郎謝克家兼太子賓客，輔太子監國，稱制行事。

translations.literal: In the second year, the emperor visited Qingcheng and ordered Privy Council Vice Director Sun Fu additionally as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Ministry of Personnel Vice Director Xie Kejia additionally as Crown Prince's Guest, to assist the crown prince in overseeing the state and acting by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the emperor went to Qingcheng and appointed privy council vice director Sun Fu as junior tutor to the crown prince and ministry of personnel vice director Xie Kejia as the crown prince's guest, to assist the crown prince in governing and acting by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金人請二帝諭太子出城。

translations.literal: Before long, the Jurchens requested the two emperors instruct the crown prince to leave the city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jurchens asked the two emperors to order the crown prince out of the city.

sentences.zh: 統制吳革力請留，欲以所募士微服衛太子潰圍以出。

translations.literal: Controller Wu Ge urgently pleaded to keep him, wishing to use recruited soldiers in plain dress to guard the crown prince and break through the encirclement to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Controller Wu Ge urgently pleaded to keep the crown prince and proposed using recruited soldiers in plain dress to escort him through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 傅不許，乃謀匿民間，別求狀類太子者並宦者二人殺之，送金人，紿以宦者竊太子欲投獻，都人爭之，並傷太子。

translations.literal: Fu would not permit it and instead plotted to hide him among the people, separately seeking one resembling the crown prince in appearance together with two eunuchs, killing them and sending them to the Jurchens, deceiving them that eunuchs had stolen the crown prince intending to surrender — the capital people struggled over it and together wounded the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused and instead plotted to hide the crown prince among the people, find a lookalike and two eunuchs, kill them, and send them to the Jurchens with a story that eunuchs had stolen the crown prince to surrender him. The capital crowd struggled over the matter and wounded the crown prince in the process.

sentences.zh: 遲疑不決者五日。

translations.literal: They hesitated and could not decide for five days.
translations.idiomatic: They hesitated for five days without deciding.

sentences.zh: 吳幵、莫儔督脅甚急，范瓊恐變生，以危言讋衛士，遂擁太子與皇后共車以出。

translations.literal: Wu Bian and Mo Chou pressed and coerced urgently; Fan Qiong feared trouble would arise and with alarming words intimidated the guards, whereupon they escorted the crown prince and empress together in one carriage to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bian and Mo Chou pressed urgently. Fan Qiong feared unrest and intimidated the guards with dire warnings, and they escorted the crown prince and empress out together in one carriage.

sentences.zh: 百官軍吏奔隨號哭，太學諸生擁拜車前，太子呼云：「百姓救我！

translations.literal: Officials and military officers ran after them wailing; Imperial Academy students pressed forward to bow before the carriage. The crown prince called out: "People of the realm, save me!
translations.idiomatic: Officials and soldiers ran after them wailing. Imperial Academy students pressed forward to bow before the carriage. The crown prince cried, "People of the realm, save me!

sentences.zh: 」哭聲震天，已而北去。

translations.literal: " Weeping shook heaven; before long they went north.
translations.idiomatic: " Weeping shook the heavens, and soon they were taken north.

sentences.zh: 弟訓。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Xun.

sentences.zh: 訓乃北地所生。

translations.literal: Xun was born in the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was born in the north.

sentences.zh: 有碭山人留遇僧者，金人見之曰：「全似趙家少帝。

translations.literal: There was a monk from Dang Mountain named Liu Yuseng; when the Jurchens saw him they said: "He looks entirely like the young emperor of the Zhao house.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from Dang Mountain named Liu Yuseng was seen by the Jurchens, who said, "He looks exactly like the Zhao young emperor.

sentences.zh: 」遇僧竊喜。

translations.literal: " Yuseng secretly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuseng secretly rejoiced at this.

sentences.zh: 紹興十年，三京路通，詔求宗室。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shaoxing, the Three Capitals route was open, and an edict sought members of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Shaoxing, when the route to the three capitals reopened, an edict sought members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 遇僧自言少帝第二子，乃守臣遣赴行在，過泗州，州官孫守信疑之，白其守，請於朝。

translations.literal: Yuseng declared himself the young emperor's second son. The defending official sent him to the mobile court; passing Si Prefecture, prefectural official Sun Shouxin doubted him, reported to his prefect, and requested instruction from court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuseng claimed to be the young emperor's second son. A defending official sent him to the mobile court. At Si Prefecture, official Sun Shouxin grew suspicious, reported to the prefect, and asked the court for instructions.

sentences.zh: 閣門言淵聖無第二子，詔寧信劾治。

translations.literal: The Gate Department said the Captive Sage had no second son; an edict ordered Ningxin to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Department reported that the captive emperor had no second son, and an edict ordered Ningxin to investigate and punish him.

sentences.zh: 遇僧伏罪，黥隸瓊州。

translations.literal: Yuseng confessed guilt and was tattooed and made a bondservant in Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuseng confessed and was tattooed and banished as a bondservant to Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後有自北至者，曰：「淵聖小大王訓，見居五國城。」

translations.literal: Later one who came from the north said: "The Captive Sage's young prince Xun now dwells in the Five States Fortress."
translations.idiomatic: Later someone arriving from the north said, "The captive emperor's young prince Xun now lives in the Five States Fortress."

sentences.zh: 元懿太子旉

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yuanyi, Fu
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yuanyi, Fu

sentences.zh: 元懿太子諱旉，高宗子也，母潘賢妃。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yuanyi, taboo name Fu, was a son of Gaozong; his mother was Worthy Consort Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yuanyi, personal name Fu, was Gaozong's son; his mother was Worthy Consort Pan.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年六月，生於南京。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Jianyan, he was born at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was born at Nanjing in the sixth month of the first year of Jianyan.

sentences.zh: 拜檢校少保、集慶軍節度使，封魏國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Guardian with honorary title and Military Commissioner of the Jiqing Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed honorary junior guardian and military commissioner of the Jiqing Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 金人侵淮南，帝幸臨安，會苗傅、劉正彥作亂，逼帝禪位於旉，改元明受。

translations.literal: The Jurchens invaded Huainan; the emperor visited Lin'an. When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, they forced the emperor to abdicate in favor of Fu and changed the era name to Mingshou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded Huainan, the emperor went to Lin'an. Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, forced him to abdicate in Fu's favor, and changed the era name to Mingshou.

sentences.zh: 既而傅等伏誅，帝復位，乃以旉為皇太子，從幸建康。

translations.literal: Before long Fu and the others were executed; the emperor resumed the throne and thereupon made Fu crown prince, following in the visit to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his associates were soon executed, the emperor resumed the throne, made Fu crown prince, and took him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 太子立，屬疾，宮人誤蹴地上金爐有聲，太子驚悸，疾轉劇，薨，諡元 懿。

translations.literal: After the crown prince was established, he fell ill. A palace woman accidentally kicked a golden censer on the floor and it made a sound; the crown prince was startled and alarmed, his illness grew severe, and he died. Posthumous title Yuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: After he was made crown prince he fell ill. A palace woman accidentally kicked a golden censer on the floor; the noise startled him, his illness worsened, and he died. He was given the posthumous title Yuanyi.

sentences.zh: 信王璩

translations.literal: Prince Xin, Qu
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin, Qu

sentences.zh: 信王璩字潤夫，初名伯玖，藝祖七世孫，秉義郎子彥之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Qu, courtesy name Runfu, original name Bojiu, seventh-generation descendant of Founder Taizu, son of Gentleman for Upholding Righteousness Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin, Qu — courtesy name Runfu, born Bojiu — was a seventh-generation descendant of Founder Taizu and son of Gentleman for Upholding Righteousness Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 生而聰慧。

translations.literal: From birth he was intelligent and clever.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 初，伯琮以宗子被選入宮，高宗命鞠於婕妤張氏；

translations.literal: At first Bocong was selected as a clansman to enter the palace; Gaozong ordered him reared by Worthy Lady Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: At first Bocong was chosen as a clansman to enter the palace, and Gaozong had him raised by Worthy Lady Zhang;

sentences.zh: 吳才人亦請於帝，遂以伯玖命才人母之，賜名璩，除和州防禦使，時生七歲矣。

translations.literal: Talented Lady Wu also requested of the emperor, and thereupon Bojiu was entrusted to the talented lady as mother, granted the name Qu, and appointed Defender of He Prefecture — he was then seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Talented Lady Wu also asked the emperor, and Bojiu was given to her to raise, granted the name Qu, and made defender of He Prefecture when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 伯琮以建國公就傅，璩獨居禁中。

translations.literal: Bocong as Duke of Jianguo took an outer tutor; Qu alone remained within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: Bocong, as Duke of Jianguo, took an outside tutor, while Qu remained alone in the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 俄拜節度使，封吳國公，宰執趙鼎、劉大中、王庶等堅持之，命不果行。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed military commissioner and enfeoffed as Duke of Wu; chief ministers Zhao Ding, Liu Dazhong, Wang Shu, and others firmly opposed it, and the order did not take effect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon to be made military commissioner and Duke of Wu, but chief ministers Zhao Ding, Liu Dazhong, Wang Shu, and others firmly opposed it, and the appointment did not go through.

sentences.zh: 會秦檜專政，遂除保大軍節度使，封崇國公。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui monopolized government, he was thereupon appointed Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui dominated the government, Qu was made military commissioner of the Baoda Army and Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 尋詔赴資善堂聽讀。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to attend lectures at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to attend lectures at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 紹興十五年，加檢校少保，進封恩平郡王，出就外第。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing, he was added as Junior Guardian with honorary title, advanced to Prince of Enping Commandery, and left to take up an outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing he was made honorary junior guardian, promoted to Prince of Enping Commandery, and moved to an outer residence.

sentences.zh: 時伯琮己封普安郡王，璩官屬禮制相等夷，號東、西府。

translations.literal: At that time Bocong had already been enfeoffed as Prince of Pu'an Commandery; Qu's offices, staff, and ritual regulations were equal, and they were called the Eastern and Western Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: By then Bocong had been made Prince of Pu'an Commandery. Qu's offices, staff, and ceremonial standing were equal, and they were called the Eastern and Western Mansions.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改武昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a year, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Wuchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made military commissioner of the Wuchang Army.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，子彥卒，璩去官持服，終喪，還舊官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Ziyan died; Qu left office to observe mourning, completed the full mourning term, and returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Ziyan died. Qu left office to mourn, completed the full mourning period, and returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后崩，普安郡王始立為皇太子，璩因加恩稱皇侄，名位始定。

translations.literal: When Grand Empress Dowager Xianren died, the Prince of Pu'an Commandery was at last established as crown prince; Qu was thereby favored and called imperial nephew, and his name and position were finally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Xianren died, the Prince of Pu'an was at last made crown prince. Qu was styled imperial nephew by special favor, and his status was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 遷開府儀同三司，判大宗正事，置司紹興府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, judged affairs of the Grand Imperial Clan Directorate, and established an office in Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, placed in charge of the Grand Imperial Clan Directorate, and given an office in Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，璩表請入賀，許之，特授少保，改靜江軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended, Qu submitted a memorial requesting to enter and offer congratulations; this was permitted, and he was specially appointed Junior Guardian and transferred to Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended, Qu asked to come and offer congratulations. Permission was granted, and he was specially made junior guardian and military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 頃之，省紹興府宗正事，改判西外宗正司。

translations.literal: Before long the Shaoxing Prefecture imperial clan affairs post was abolished, and he was transferred to judge the Western Outer Imperial Clan Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Shaoxing prefectural imperial clan post was abolished, and he was transferred to the Western Outer Imperial Clan Bureau.

sentences.zh: 璩累章乞閑，改醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Qu repeatedly submitted memorials begging for leisure and was transferred to Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Qu repeatedly asked to retire and was made commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，除少傅。

translations.literal: During Chunxi, he was appointed Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi he was made junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，奔赴得疾，逾年而薨，年五十九，追封信王，累贈太保、太師。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, Qu rushed to attend and fell ill; after more than a year he died, aged fifty-nine. Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Xin, cumulatively promoted to Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Qu hurried to attend the funeral and fell ill. He died a year later at fifty-nine, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Xin, and was later promoted to grand guardian and grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 始，璩之入宮也，儲位未定者垂三十年，中外頗以為疑。

translations.literal: At the beginning, from Qu's entry into the palace, the heir's position was unsettled for nearly thirty years, and inside and outside the court there was considerable doubt.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Qu entered the palace, the succession remained unsettled for nearly thirty years, and court and country were full of uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 孝宗既立，天性友愛，璩入朝，屢召宴內殿，呼以官，不名也，賜予無算。

translations.literal: After Xiaozong was established, by nature he was friendly and affectionate; when Qu entered court, he was repeatedly summoned to feast in the inner hall, addressed by his office title and not by name, and given rewards beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaozong was established, his nature was warm and affectionate. When Qu came to court, he was repeatedly summoned to feasts in the inner hall, addressed by title rather than by name, and given lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 子四人：師淳歷忠州團練使、永州防禦使，師灝、師淪、師路並補武翼大夫。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Shichun successively served as Regimentation Commissioner of Zhong Prefecture and Defender of Yong Prefecture; Shihao, Shilun, and Shilu were all appointed Military Attendant of the Martial Wings.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Shichun served as regimentation commissioner of Zhong Prefecture and defender of Yong Prefecture; Shihao, Shilun, and Shilu were all appointed military attendants of the martial wings.

sentences.zh: 孫希楙，特補保義郎。

translations.literal: His grandson Ximao was specially appointed Gentleman for Upholding Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ximao was specially appointed Gentleman for Upholding Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 莊文太子愭

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhuangwen, Kui
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangwen, Kui

sentences.zh: 莊文太子諱愭，孝宗嫡長子也，母郭皇后。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhuangwen, taboo name Kui, was Xiaozong's eldest son by the primary wife; his mother was Empress Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangwen, personal name Kui, was Xiaozong's eldest son by his primary wife, Empress Guo.

sentences.zh: 初名愉，補右內率府副率，尋賜名愭，除右監門衛大將軍、榮州刺史。

translations.literal: His original name was Yu; he was appointed Deputy Director of the Right Inner Rate Office, soon granted the name Kui, and appointed Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Prefect of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yu. He was appointed deputy director of the Right Inner Rate Office, soon granted the name Kui, and made grand general of the Right Gate Guard and prefect of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝宗為皇子時，愭拜蘄州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was still a prince, Kui was appointed Defender of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong was still a prince, Kui was made defender of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，除少保、永興軍節度使，封鄧王。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Kui was appointed Junior Guardian and Military Commissioner of the Yongxing Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne, Kui was made junior guardian and military commissioner of the Yongxing Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 故事，皇子出閣，封王，兼兩鎮，然後加司空。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a prince left the palace quarters he was enfeoffed as prince, given two circuits concurrently, and only then added as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a prince left the inner palace he was enfeoffed as prince, given two circuits, and only then made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 愭自防禦使躐拜少保，章異數也。

translations.literal: Kui leaped from defender directly to junior guardian — a departure from the regular order.
translations.idiomatic: Kui leaped from defender straight to junior guardian — an exceptional promotion.

sentences.zh: 太子賢厚，上皇與帝皆愛之。

translations.literal: The crown prince was worthy and generous; both the Retired Emperor and the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was worthy and generous, and both the retired emperor and the emperor loved him.

sentences.zh: 帝從禮官議服期，以日易月；

translations.literal: The emperor followed the ritual officials' deliberation to observe one-year mourning, substituting days for months;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed the ritual officials and observed one-year mourning, counting days in place of months;

sentences.zh: 文武百官服衰，服一日而除；

translations.literal: civil and military officials wore mourning garments, wearing them for one day and then removing them;
translations.idiomatic: civil and military officials wore mourning for one day and then removed it;

sentences.zh: 東宮臣僚齊衰三月，臨七日而除。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace staff wore three months of coarse hemp, removing it after seven days of mourning attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace staff wore coarse hemp for three months and ended mourning after seven days of attendance.

sentences.zh: 比葬，帝再至東宮，命宰臣奉諡冊，大小祥皆以執政官行禮。

translations.literal: By the time of burial, the emperor again visited the Eastern Palace, ordered the chief minister to present the posthumous edict, and for both greater and lesser auspices had administering officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: By the burial, the emperor visited the Eastern Palace again, had the chief minister present the posthumous edict, and had administering officials perform the greater and lesser mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 子挺，錢氏所生也，甫晬，除福州觀察使，封榮國公，乾道九年卒，贈武當軍節度使，追封豫國公。

translations.literal: His son Ting, born of Lady Qian, was just past infancy when appointed Military Commissioner of Observation for Fuzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong; he died in the ninth year of Qiandao, was posthumously given the Wudang Army, and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ting, born of Lady Qian, was barely past infancy when made military commissioner of observation for Fuzhou and Duke of Rong. He died in the ninth year of Qiandao, and was posthumously made military commissioner of the Wudang Army and Duke of Yu.

sentences.zh: 寧宗時，命宗子希基為太子後。

translations.literal: During Ningzong's reign, an order was issued for clansman Xiji to succeed as the crown prince's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ningzong, clansman Xiji was appointed to succeed the crown prince's line.

sentences.zh: 希基，藝祖九世孫也，賜名搢，補右千牛衛將軍，置教授於府。

translations.literal: Xiji was a ninth-generation descendant of Founder Taizu; granted the name Jin, appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and given instructors in his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji was a ninth-generation descendant of Founder Taizu. He was granted the name Jin, appointed general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and given instructors at his residence.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，除忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi, he was appointed Defender of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaixi he was made defender of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉定八年，更名思正。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiading, his name was changed to Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiading his name was changed to Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 魏惠憲王愷

translations.literal: Prince Wei the Kind and Worthy, Kai
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei the Kind and Worthy, Kai

sentences.zh: 魏惠憲王諱愷，莊文同母弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Wei the Kind and Worthy, taboo name Kai, was Zhuangwen's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei the Kind and Worthy, personal name Kai, was Zhuangwen's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 初補右內率府副率，轉右監門衛大將軍、貴州團練使。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Deputy Director of the Right Inner Rate Office, then transferred to Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Regimentation Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was first deputy director of the Right Inner Rate Office, then grand general of the Right Gate Guard and regimentation commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，拜雄武軍節度使、開府儀同三司，封慶王。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, Kai was appointed Military Commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne, Kai was made military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, and Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 莊文太子薨，愷次當立，帝意未決。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhuangwen died, Kai was next in line to be established, but the emperor's mind was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhuangwen died, Kai was next in line, but the emperor had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 既而以恭王英武類己，竟立之。

translations.literal: Thereupon, because Prince Gong was martial and resembled himself, he ultimately established him.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Prince Gong martial and like himself, he ultimately chose him instead.

sentences.zh: 加愷雄武、保寧軍節度使，進封魏王，判寧國府。

translations.literal: Kai was added as Military Commissioner of the Xiongwu and Baoning armies and advanced to Prince of Wei, judging affairs of the Ningguo prefectural establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was given the Xiongwu and Baoning armies, made Prince of Wei, and placed in charge of the Ningguo prefectural establishment.

sentences.zh: 妻華國夫人韋氏，特封韓、魏兩國夫人，以示優禮。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady of Huaguo, the Wei clan, was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Han and Wei, to show exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Wei of Huaguo, was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Han and Wei as a mark of exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金三千兩、白金一萬兩，命宰執設於玉津園，王登車，顧謂虞允文曰：「更望相公保全。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand taels of gold and ten thousand taels of silver; the chief ministers were ordered to set them out at Jade Ford Garden. As the prince mounted his carriage he turned and said to Yu Yunwen: "I hope again that the Chancellor will preserve me.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three thousand taels of gold and ten thousand taels of silver, with the chief ministers to set them out at Jade Ford Garden. As the prince mounted his carriage he said to Yu Yunwen, "I still hope the chancellor will protect me.

sentences.zh: 」比至鎮，奏朝天申節，許之。

translations.literal: " When he reached his command, he memorialized to attend court on the Tian Shen festival day, and this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching his post, he asked to attend court on the Tian Shen festival day, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 府長史上言，欲與司馬分治郡，俾王受成。

translations.literal: The prefectural chief administrator memorialized, wishing to divide governance of the commandery with the marshal so the prince would receive completed reports.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural chief administrator proposed dividing commandery governance with the marshal so the prince would receive completed reports.

sentences.zh: 愷奏曰：「臣被命判府，今專委長史、司馬，是處臣無用之地。

translations.literal: Kai memorialized: "Your servant was ordered to judge the prefectural establishment; now entrusting it solely to the chief administrator and marshal is to place your servant where he is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Kai memorialized, "I was ordered to oversee this prefectural establishment. Entrusting everything to the chief administrator and marshal leaves me with nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 況一郡置三判府，臣恐吏民紛競不一，徒見其擾。

translations.literal: Moreover, with three judges over one commandery, your servant fears officials and people will compete and not be of one mind, only seeing disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, three judges over one commandery will only breed rivalry and disorder among officials and people.

sentences.zh: 長史、司馬宜主錢穀、 訟牒，俾擬呈臣依而判之，庶上下安，事益易治。

translations.literal: The chief administrator and marshal should handle funds, grain, and litigation documents, drafting them for presentation so your servant may approve them — then above and below will be at peace and affairs easier to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator and marshal should handle revenue, grain, and legal papers and submit drafts for my approval. That way affairs will run smoothly above and below.

sentences.zh: 」又請增士人貢額。

translations.literal: " He also requested increasing the quota of presented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to increase the quota of presented scholars.

sentences.zh: 朝廷悉從之。

translations.literal: The court fully acceded.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all his requests.

sentences.zh: 愷究心民事，築圩田之隤圮者，帝手詔嘉勞之。

translations.literal: Kai devoted himself to the people's affairs and repaired collapsed polder dikes; the emperor personally wrote an edict commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai devoted himself to local welfare and repaired collapsed polder dikes. The emperor wrote a personal edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，徙判明州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi, he was transferred to judge Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunxi he was transferred to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 輟屬邑田租以贍學。

translations.literal: He suspended subordinate district land rents to support schools.
translations.idiomatic: He suspended subordinate district land rents to support the schools.

sentences.zh: 得兩歧麥，圖以獻，帝復賜手詔曰：「汝勸課藝植，農不遊惰，宜獲瑞麥之應。

translations.literal: He obtained double-eared wheat and sent a diagram as tribute; the emperor again bestowed a personal edict saying: "You urged farming and planting; the farmers did not wander idle — it is fitting you should receive this auspicious wheat in response.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained double-eared wheat and sent a diagram as tribute. The emperor wrote again, "You urged farming and diligence; it is fitting that auspicious wheat should appear in response.

sentences.zh: 」加愷荊南、集慶軍節度使，行江陵尹，尋改永興、成德軍 節度使、揚州牧。

translations.literal: " Kai was added as Military Commissioner of the Jingnan and Jiqing armies, acting as Prefect of Jiangling, soon transferred to Military Commissioner of the Yongxing and Chengde armies and Governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was given the Jingnan and Jiqing armies and made acting prefect of Jiangling, then military commissioner of the Yongxing and Chengde armies and governor of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，薨於明州，年三十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he died at Ming Prefecture, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at Ming Prefecture, aged thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝素服發哀於別殿，贈淮南武寧軍節度使、揚州牧兼徐州牧，諡惠寧。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain robes and expressed mourning in a side hall, posthumously appointing him Military Commissioner of the Huainan and Wuning armies and Governor of Yang and Xu Prefectures, posthumous title Huining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned in plain robes in a side hall, posthumously made him military commissioner of the Huainan and Wuning armies and governor of Yang and Xu, with the posthumous title Huining.

sentences.zh: 王性寬慈，上皇雅愛之。

translations.literal: The prince was by nature generous and kind; the Retired Emperor greatly loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was generous by nature, and the retired emperor loved him deeply.

sentences.zh: 雖以宗社大計出王於外，然心每念之，賜賚不絕。
