translations.literal: Although for the great design of the altars of state he was sent outside the capital, his heart always thought of him and gifts never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Although the realm's needs sent him out of the capital, the emperor never ceased to think of him or to send gifts.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝泫然曰：「向所以越次建儲者，正為此子福氣差薄耳！

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, the emperor said with tears: "The reason I passed over the proper order in establishing the heir was precisely because this son's fortune was rather thin!
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the emperor wept and said, "The reason I passed over him when choosing an heir was that this son's fortune was too thin!

sentences.zh: 」治二郡有仁聲，薨之日，四明父老乞建祠立碑，以紀遺愛。

translations.literal: " In governing the two commanderies he had a reputation for benevolence; on the day of his death, the elders of Siming begged to build a shrine and erect a stele to record his lingering affection.
translations.idiomatic: He governed two commanderies with a reputation for benevolence. On the day he died, elders of Siming asked to build a shrine and stele to his memory.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 攄早卒。

translations.literal: Shu died early.
translations.idiomatic: Shu died young.

sentences.zh: 抦生於明州，母卜氏，信安郡夫人，王薨，還居行在。

translations.literal: Bing was born at Ming Prefecture; his mother was the Bu clan, Lady of Xin'an Commandery; when the prince died, they returned to dwell at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was born at Ming Prefecture to Lady Bu of Xin'an Commandery. After the prince's death they returned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 抦性早慧，帝愛之，將內禪，升耀州觀察使，封嘉國公。

translations.literal: Bing was clever from youth and the emperor loved him; when about to abdicate internally, he was promoted to Military Commissioner of Observation for Yao Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was clever from youth and the emperor loved him. As the emperor prepared to abdicate, Bing was made military commissioner of observation for Yao Prefecture and Duke of Jia.

sentences.zh: 慶元間，封吳興郡王，領昭慶軍節度使。

translations.literal: During the Qingyuan era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuxing Commandery and held the Zhaqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingyuan he was made Prince of Wuxing Commandery and given the Zhaqing Army.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年薨，贈太保，封沂王，諡靖惠。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaixi, was posthumously made Grand Guardian, enfeoffed as Prince of Yi, posthumous title Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaixi, was posthumously made grand guardian, enfeoffed as Prince of Yi, and given the posthumous title Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 子垓，三歲而夭。

translations.literal: His son Gai died at three years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai died at age three.

sentences.zh: 詔立宗室希瞿子為其後，更名均，領右千牛衛將軍，置教授於府。

translations.literal: An edict established clansman Xiqu's son as his heir, renamed Jun, appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and placed instructors in the residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made clansman Xiqu's son his heir, renamed him Jun, appointed him general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and placed instructors at the residence.

sentences.zh: 尋加福州觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as Military Commissioner of Observation for Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made military commissioner of observation for Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後更名貴和，即鎮王竑也。

translations.literal: Later his name was changed to Guihe — this is Prince Zhen Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later renamed Guihe — Prince Zhen, Hong.

sentences.zh: 景獻太子詢

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jingxian, Xun
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingxian, Xun

sentences.zh: 景獻太子諱詢，燕懿王後，藝祖十一世孫也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jingxian, taboo name Xun, was heir to Prince Yan the Worthy; an eleventh-generation descendant of Founder Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingxian, personal name Xun, was heir to Prince Yan the Worthy and an eleventh-generation descendant of Founder Taizu.

sentences.zh: 初名與願。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yuyuan.

sentences.zh: 寧宗既失袞王，從宰執京鏜等請，取與願養於宮中，年六歲，賜名嚴，除福州觀察使。

translations.literal: After Ningzong lost the heir-apparent prince, at the request of chief minister Jing Tang and others, Yuyuan was taken to be reared in the palace at age six, granted the name Yan, and appointed Military Commissioner of Observation for Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Ningzong lost his heir, at chief minister Jing Tang's request Yuyuan was brought into the palace at age six, given the name Yan, and made military commissioner of observation for Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，拜威武軍節度使，封衛國公，聽讀資善堂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Weiwu Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, and permitted to study at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiatai he was made military commissioner of the Weiwu Army, Duke of Wei, and allowed to study at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，時邊事益急，金人請誅首謀用兵者，嚴用翊善史彌遠計，奏韓侂胄輕起兵端，上危宗社，宜賜黜罷，以安邊境。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi, as border affairs grew urgent, the Jin demanded execution of those who first advocated war. Yan used the plan of his tutor Shi Miyuan and memorialized that Han Tuozhou had lightly raised troops, endangering the altars of state — he should be dismissed to pacify the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi, as the border crisis sharpened, the Jin demanded the execution of those who had advocated war. Yan, using his tutor Shi Miyuan's plan, memorialized that Han Tuozhou had rashly raised troops and endangered the realm and should be dismissed to pacify the frontier.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嚴立為皇太子，拜開府儀同三司，封榮王，更為幬。

translations.literal: Yan was established as crown prince, appointed Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Prince of Rong, and renamed Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was made crown prince, given commissioner with the protocol of the three excellencies, enfeoffed as Prince of Rong, and renamed Chou.

sentences.zh: 詔禦朝太子侍立，宰執日赴資善堂會議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the crown prince to attend court standing in attendance, and chief ministers daily to attend deliberations at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was ordered to attend court standing, and chief ministers to meet daily at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 尋用天禧故事，宰輔大臣並兼師傅、賓客，太子出居東宮，更名詢。

translations.literal: Soon, following the Tianxi precedent, chief ministers and great officials all additionally served as tutors and guests; the crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace and was renamed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, following Tianxi precedent, chief ministers also served as his tutors and guests. The crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace and was renamed Xun.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年薨，年二十九，諡景獻。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Jiading, aged twenty-nine; posthumous title Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Jiading at twenty-nine, with the posthumous title Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 鎮王竑

translations.literal: Prince Zhen, Hong
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen, Hong

sentences.zh: 鎮王竑，希瞿之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen Hong was the son of Xiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen, Hong, was Xiqu's son.

sentences.zh: 初，沂靖惠王薨，無嗣，以竑為之後，賜名均，尋改賜名貴和。

translations.literal: At first, when Prince Yi Jinghui died without an heir, Hong was made his successor, granted the name Jun, soon changed to Guihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi Jinghui died without an heir, Hong was made his successor, given the name Jun, then renamed Guihe.

sentences.zh: 太子詢薨，乃立貴和為皇子，賜名竑，授寧武軍節度使，封祁國公。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun died, Guihe was thereupon established as imperial son, granted the name Hong, appointed Military Commissioner of the Ningwu Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun died, Guihe was made imperial son, renamed Hong, given the Ningwu Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十五年五月，加檢校少保，封濟國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year of Jiading, he was added as Junior Guardian with honorary title and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year of Jiading he was made honorary junior guardian and Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 竑好鼓琴，丞相史彌遠買美人善琴者，納諸御，而厚廩其家，使美人間竑，動息必以告。

translations.literal: Hong loved playing the zither; Chancellor Shi Miyuan bought a beautiful woman skilled at the zither and presented her to the palace, richly supporting her family so the woman would spy on Hong and report his every movement.
translations.idiomatic: Hong loved the zither. Chancellor Shi Miyuan bought a skilled female player, presented her to the palace, and richly supported her family so she would spy on Hong and report his every move.

sentences.zh: 美人知書慧黠，竑嬖之。

translations.literal: The woman was literate and clever; Hong doted on her.
translations.idiomatic: She was literate and clever, and Hong favored her.

sentences.zh: 宮壁有輿地圖，竑指瓊厓曰：「吾他日得志，置史彌遠於此。

translations.literal: On a palace wall was a map of the realm; Hong pointed to Qiongya and said: "When I achieve my aim someday, I will place Shi Miyuan there.
translations.idiomatic: On a palace wall was a map of the realm. Hong pointed to Qiongya and said, "When I come to power I will banish Shi Miyuan there.

sentences.zh: 」又嘗呼彌遠為「新恩」。

translations.literal: " He also once called Miyuan "New Favor."
translations.idiomatic: He also called Miyuan "New Favor."

sentences.zh: 以他日非新州則恩州也。

translations.literal: Meaning that someday it would be either Xin Prefecture or En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning exile to either Xin or En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彌遠聞之，嘗因七月七日進乞巧奇玩以覘之，竑乘酒碎於地。

translations.literal: When Miyuan heard this, on the seventh day of the seventh month he presented curious objects for the Begging-for-Skill festival to probe him; Hong, drunk, smashed them on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Miyuan on the Qixi festival sent curious gifts to test him; Hong, drunk, smashed them on the floor.

sentences.zh: 彌遠大懼，日夕思以處竑，而竑不知也。

translations.literal: Miyuan was greatly afraid and day and night thought how to deal with Hong, while Hong did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was terrified and plotted day and night against Hong, who knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 時沂王猶未有後，方選宗室希盧子昀繼之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Yi still had no heir; they were selecting clansman Xilu's son Yun to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi still had no heir; clansman Xilu's son Yun was being chosen to succeed.

sentences.zh: 一日，彌遠為其父飯僧淨慈寺，獨與國子學錄鄭清之登惠日閣，屏人語曰：「皇子不堪負荷，聞後沂邸者甚賢，今欲擇講官，君其善訓迪之。

translations.literal: One day Miyuan was feeding monks for his father at Jingci Temple and, alone with Imperial College Recorder Zheng Qingzhi, ascended Huiri Pavilion. Sending attendants away, he said: "The imperial son cannot bear the burden. I hear the next Prince of Yi household is very worthy. I now wish to choose a lecturing official — you must instruct and guide him well.
translations.idiomatic: One day Miyuan was sponsoring monks for his father at Jingci Temple. Alone with imperial college recorder Zheng Qingzhi on Huiri Pavilion, he dismissed attendants and said, "The imperial son cannot bear the burden. The next Prince of Yi heir is very worthy. Choose a lecturer and train him well.

sentences.zh: 事成，彌遠之坐即君坐也。

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, the seat Miyuan occupies will be your seat.
translations.idiomatic: If this succeeds, my seat will be yours.

sentences.zh: 然言出於彌遠之口，入於君之耳，若一語泄者，吾與君皆族矣。

translations.literal: Yet if a single word leaks from Miyuan's mouth into your ear, you and I will both be executed to the last of our clans.
translations.idiomatic: But if one word leaks from my mouth to yours, our clans will be exterminated.

sentences.zh: 」清之拱手曰：「不敢。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi bowed with hands joined and said: "I dare not.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi bowed and said, "I dare not.

sentences.zh: 」乃以清之兼魏忠憲王府教授。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Qingzhi was additionally appointed lecturer to the Wei Zhongxian Wang princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was then additionally appointed lecturer to the Yi Jinghui princely household.

sentences.zh: 清之日教昀為文，又購高宗書俾習焉。

translations.literal: Qingzhi daily taught Yun composition and also purchased Gaozong's calligraphy for him to practice.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi taught Yun composition daily and bought Gaozong's calligraphy for him to practice.

sentences.zh: 清之上謁彌遠，即以昀詩文翰墨以示，彌遠譽之不容口。

translations.literal: Qingzhi attended Miyuan and showed Yun's poetry, essays, and calligraphy; Miyuan praised them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi showed Miyuan Yun's poetry and calligraphy, which Miyuan praised without end.

sentences.zh: 彌遠嘗問清之：「吾聞其賢已熟，大要竟何如？

translations.literal: Miyuan once asked Qingzhi: "I have long heard he is worthy — in the main, what is he finally like?
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan once asked Qingzhi, "I have long heard he is worthy — what is he really like?

sentences.zh: 」清之曰：「其人之賢，更僕不能數，然一言以斷之曰：不凡。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi said: "This man's worthiness cannot be numbered in repeated accounts — yet to sum it in one phrase: not ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "His virtues are countless, but in one word: not ordinary.

sentences.zh: 」彌遠頷之再三，策立之意益堅。

translations.literal: " Miyuan nodded again and again; his intent to establish Yun grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan nodded repeatedly, and his resolve to make Yun heir grew firm.

sentences.zh: 清之始以小官兼教授，其後累遷，兼如故。

translations.literal: Qingzhi at first held a minor post concurrently as lecturer; afterward he was repeatedly promoted while still holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi began as a minor official concurrently lecturing and kept the post through later promotions.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，彌遠始遣清之往，告昀以將立之之意。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, Miyuan at last sent Qingzhi to inform Yun of the intent to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died, Miyuan sent Qingzhi to tell Yun he was to be established.

sentences.zh: 再三言之，昀默然不應。

translations.literal: He spoke of it again and again; Yun remained silent and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi spoke repeatedly; Yun remained silent.

sentences.zh: 最後清之乃言曰：「丞相以清之從遊之久，故使布腹心於足下。

translations.literal: Finally Qingzhi said: "The Chancellor, because Qingzhi has long studied with you, sends me to lay bare his heart to you.
translations.idiomatic: At last Qingzhi said, "Because I have long been your teacher, the chancellor sends me to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 今足下不答一語，則清之將何以覆命於丞相？

translations.literal: Now you answer not a single word — how shall Qingzhi report back to the Chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: You have not answered a word — how am I to report back?

sentences.zh: 」昀始拱手徐答曰：「紹興老母在。

translations.literal: " Yun at last bowed with hands joined and slowly replied: "My old mother is at Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yun at last bowed slowly and said, "My old mother is at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 」清之以告彌遠，益相與歎其不凡。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi reported this to Miyuan, and they admired his extraordinariness all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi reported this, and they admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 竑跂足以需宣召，久而不至。

translations.literal: Hong stood on tiptoe awaiting the summons, but for a long time it did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Hong stood on tiptoe awaiting the summons, but it did not come.

sentences.zh: 彌遠在禁中，遣快行宣皇子，令之曰：「今所宣是沂靖惠王府皇子，非萬歲巷皇子，苟誤，則汝曹皆處斬。

translations.literal: Miyuan was in the Forbidden City and sent a fast courier to announce the imperial son, telling him: "The one announced today is the Prince of Yi Jinghui household's imperial son, not the Wansui Lane imperial son. If you err, you will all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan, inside the Forbidden City, sent a fast courier with orders: "Announce the Prince of Yi Jinghui's son, not the Wansui Lane prince. If you err, you will all be executed.

sentences.zh: 」竑不能自己，屬目牆壁間，見快行過其府而不入，疑焉。

translations.literal: " Hong could not restrain himself and, fixing his gaze on the wall, saw the fast courier pass his mansion without entering and grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Hong watched anxiously and saw the courier pass his mansion without entering, and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 己而擁一人徑過，天已暝，不知其為誰，甚惑。

translations.literal: Before long someone was escorted straight past; it was already dark and he did not know who it was — he was deeply perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone was escorted past in the dusk; he could not tell who it was and was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 帝輟朝，賻銀絹各一千、會子萬貫，贈少師、保靜鎮潼軍節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor halted court and granted one thousand taels of silver and silk each, ten thousand strings of treasury notes, posthumously appointing Junior Tutor and Military Commissioner of the Baojing Zhentong Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted court and granted a thousand taels of silver and silk and ten thousand strings of treasury notes, posthumously making him junior tutor and military commissioner of the Baojing Zhentong Army.

sentences.zh: 給事中盛章、權直舍人院王塈一再繳奏，詔從之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Sheng Zhang and Acting Drafting Academician Wang Qi memorialized objections twice; an edict followed their remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Sheng Zhang and acting drafting academician Wang Qi objected twice; the edict was withdrawn as they urged.

sentences.zh: 右正言李知孝累奏，追奪王爵，降封巴陵縣公。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Li Zhixiao memorialized repeatedly; the court posthumously stripped his princely rank and demoted him to Duke of Baling County.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrator Li Zhixiao memorialized repeatedly; Hong's princely rank was stripped and he was demoted to Duke of Baling County.

sentences.zh: 於是在廷之臣真德秀、魏了翁、洪諮夔、胡夢昱等每以竑為言，彌遠輒惡而斥遠之。

translations.literal: At this time court ministers Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Hong Zai, Hu Mengyu, and others often spoke on Hong's behalf; Miyuan always hated this and banished them far away.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers such as Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Hong Zai, and Hu Mengyu often spoke for Hong; Miyuan hated this and banished them.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping, an edict restored his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping an edict restored his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 妻吳氏為比丘尼，賜惠淨法空大師，月給缽錢百貫。

translations.literal: His wife the Wu clan became a Buddhist nun, granted the dharma name Huijing Fakong Great Master, with a monthly allowance of a hundred strings for her bowl.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wu became a nun, granted the dharma name Huijing Fakong Great Master, with a monthly allowance of a hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，度宗降詔，追復元贈節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding, Emperor Duzong issued an edict posthumously restoring his original honorary military commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingding, Emperor Duzong restored his original honorary military commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，提領戶部財用兼修國史常楙請立竑後，試禮部侍郎兼中書舍人王應麟請更封大國，表墓錫諡，命大宗正司議選擇立后，迎善氣，銷惡運，莫先於此。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou, Director of Palace Treasury and Concurrent Compiler of National History Chang Mao requested establishing an heir for Hong; Acting Vice Minister of Rites and Concurrent Drafting Academician Wang Yinglin requested re-enfeoffing him as a great state, marking his tomb, and granting a posthumous title — ordering the Grand Imperial Clan Directorate to select and establish a successor, welcome good qi, and dispel ill fortune — nothing should come before this.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Deyou, Chang Mao asked to establish an heir for Hong; Wang Yinglin asked to re-enfeoff him as a great prince, mark his tomb, and grant a posthumous title, and have the Grand Imperial Clan Directorate choose a successor — nothing was more urgent for restoring fortune.

sentences.zh: 下禮部議，贈太師、尚書令，依舊節度使，升封鎮王，諡昭肅。

translations.literal: It was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation: posthumously Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, retaining the former military commissioner rank, advanced to Prince Zhen, posthumous title Zhaosu.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites deliberated: posthumously grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat, with his former military commissioner rank, raised to Prince Zhen, posthumous title Zhaosu.

sentences.zh: 以田萬畝賜其家，遣應麟致祭。

translations.literal: Ten thousand mu of fields were granted to his family, and Yinglin was dispatched to perform the sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand mu of fields were granted to his family, and Wang Yinglin was sent to perform the sacrificial rites.
